Q: How to de-select a row for deletion on PhpStorm's internal SQL table view interface A:

In PhpStorm, to unmark or revert a specific row's deletion without cancelling the entire batch, select that specific row and press Ctrl + Alt + Z (or Cmd + Option + Z on Mac) to perform a Revert Selected.

I found that pressing CTRL + ALT + Z and clicking on the row on PhpStorm correctly reverted the deletion selection.

Q: Enumerate allocated objects A:

There are potentially two forms of memory lose

  1. Memory that was allocated, but it is no longer referenced from any place... and so it will not be possible to delete it. This is a proper leak. In Linux, the main tool of choice is valgrind. Valgrind is a framework for multiple tools. The tool you would be after is memcheck.... This is a dynamic analysis tool that will report about leaks and other memory problems. This goes further than enumerating the memory allocated, but it also needs to check whether it is still referenced or not.
  2. Memory that was allocated and it is still referenced, but somehow you've forgotten about it (e.g. vectors that grow endlessly because no-one never removes from them). This is where you need a tool for telling you the composition of all the memory you've allocated. Again valgrind can help you here. The tool this time is called massif

I'm sure there are more tools out there. These are pretty popular.

In Solaris, I'd recommend libumem for leak tracking and analyzer in Sun's Studio for profiling and memory analysis.

Q: How to run a sudo command silently on the server? A:

If you want to do this from Linux machine, you can write a script with:

sshpass -p "PASSWORD" user@server

and give only execute permission.
